# Local QA (format, lint, and test)

Run the local QA script `scripts/qa.sh` in this skill.

## Procedure

- Execute the script exactly as shown above when this skill is triggered.
- Capture and summarize key output (success/failure, major warnings, and any files modified).
- If the script fails due to missing tooling (`command not found`, missing executable, or equivalent), install the missing tool(s) and rerun `./scripts/qa.sh`.
- Install tools using this order of preference:
  1. Use the project's package manager when applicable (`uv`/`poetry` for Python, package manager scripts/dependencies for Node.js).
  2. Use a system package manager (`brew` on macOS, `apt` on Debian/Ubuntu) when project-local install is not applicable.
  3. Use language-specific installers as fallback (`pipx`/`pip`, `npm`, `go install`, etc.).
- If multiple tools are missing, repeat install -> rerun until QA completes or you hit a blocker.
- If installation fails or requires unavailable privileges, report what was attempted, the exact failure, and stop.
- Do not run unrelated commands; only run commands needed for QA and missing-tool installation.

# opencode-action

Run an [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) agent from GitHub Actions, including inline pull request review comments, pull request reviews, and manually dispatched tasks.

[![CI](https://github.com/dceoy/opencode-action/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dceoy/opencode-action/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## Quick start

### 1. Add a provider secret

In **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, add the API key for your model provider. The example below uses `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.

### 2. Add the workflow

Create `.github/workflows/opencode.yml`:

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode
on:
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  opencode:
    if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '/oc') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/opencode')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run OpenCode
        uses: dceoy/opencode-action@ab6604cc588b61690c4eae15b4a9682c5c47f011
        env:
          OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        with:
          model: opencode-go/kimi-k3
```

### 3. Add an inline comment to a pull request diff

```text
/opencode explain this change
```

The shorter `/oc` trigger also works:

```text
/oc suggest a fix
```

The default setup exchanges the workflow OIDC token for an OpenCode GitHub App token, which requires `id-token: write`.

On v2, no GitHub credentials are passed to OpenCode through its environment, and `gh` runs unauthenticated. In the default OIDC mode, the launcher only posts the final message as a reply to the review-comment thread. For code-writing runs, set `use-github-token: true` with persisted checkout credentials and a write-capable token (enabling `git push`), or use `runtime: v1` with an exact v1 pin. In token mode, persisted checkout credentials remain readable from OpenCode's shell, so that token is not isolated from the model; scope it least-privilege.

## Reusable workflows

For smaller caller workflows, this repository provides reusable workflows for OpenCode tasks and pull request reviews:

| Workflow                                                       | Purpose                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`opencode-bot.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-bot.yml)       | Run OpenCode via PR review comments, dispatch, or a fixed prompt.                 |
| [`opencode-review.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml) | Install and use `pr-loop`'s external `pr-review` skill for `pull_request` events. |

See [Reusable workflows](docs/reusable-workflows.md) for caller examples, inputs, secrets, and permission requirements.

## Models and secrets

Set `model` to a `provider/model` value and pass the corresponding API key:

| Provider        | Example model                | Secret               |
| --------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------- |
| OpenCode        | `opencode-go/kimi-k3`        | `OPENCODE_API_KEY`   |
| OpenRouter      | `openrouter/openrouter/free` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| Anthropic       | `anthropic/claude-opus-5`    | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`  |
| OpenAI          | `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`         | `OPENAI_API_KEY`     |
| Custom provider | `myprovider/my-model`        | Provider-specific    |

The provider account must have sufficient credits or quota. For providers not built into OpenCode, see [Custom providers](docs/custom-providers.md).

## Sakura AI Engine model synchronization

The optional [Sakura model synchronization workflow](.github/workflows/sync-sakura-models.yml) discovers chat-capable Sakura AI Engine models and opens or updates a pull request when the catalog changes. Configure the `SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY` repository secret before enabling it.

The workflow uses the repository-provided `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; no additional GitHub token secret is required. GitHub does not create new workflow runs for events triggered by `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so pull requests created by this workflow do not automatically trigger `pull_request` workflows. See [GitHub's `GITHUB_TOKEN` documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token).

## Releases

The [release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml) runs every Monday at 09:15 JST when eligible files have changed, or manually for major, minor, and patch releases. After publication, it updates the major-version tag and opens a PR to refresh SHA pins.

## Inputs

| Input                 | Default                   | Description                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`               | Required                  | Model in `provider/model` format.                                                                                                                 |
| `agent`               | `build`                   | Primary agent. A slash command can override it.                                                                                                   |
| `prompt`              | Event comment             | Fixed prompt to use instead of the triggering comment.                                                                                            |
| `mentions`            | `/opencode,/oc`           | Comma-separated trigger phrases.                                                                                                                  |
| `variant`             | -                         | Provider-specific reasoning effort; leave empty unless supported. See [Custom providers](docs/custom-providers.md#variants-for-custom-providers). |
| `share`               | `false`                   | Share the OpenCode session.                                                                                                                       |
| `use-github-token`    | `false`                   | Use the workflow token instead of the default App-token flow.                                                                                     |
| `runtime`             | `v2`                      | Runtime generation: `v1` or `v2`.                                                                                                                 |
| `opencode-version`    | `v2.3.0`                  | Exact stable release matching the runtime. The Sakura provider requires 1.2.25+.                                                                  |
| `use-bundled-toolkit` | `true`                    | Install the bundled provider configuration for normal runs or the trusted review bridge for review-only runs.                                     |
| `review-only`         | `false`                   | Enable isolated review execution and install upstream `pr-review`.                                                                                |
| `pr-review-ref`       | Caller-supplied SHA       | Immutable `pr-loop` commit supplying the review skill.                                                                                            |
| `timeout-minutes`     | `60`                      | Stop OpenCode after this many minutes.                                                                                                            |
| `oidc-base-url`       | `https://api.opencode.ai` | OIDC exchange URL for a custom GitHub App installation.                                                                                           |

The default is the Renovate-managed OpenCode v2 pin. Floating versions, including `latest`, are rejected. To use v1, set `runtime: v1` and a matching exact pin such as `v1.19.3`; test and pin upgrades for the selected major.

Direct `workflow_dispatch` uses the same inputs as `workflow_call`; `model` and a non-empty `prompt` are required to run the job.

When `use-github-token: true`, keep `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `env` and grant only the permissions needed for the task. On v2, the token is not placed in OpenCode's environment and `gh` is unauthenticated; the launcher uses it for thread replies. In token mode, the persisted checkout credential remains readable from the shell (`git push`), so use a least-privilege token.

Outputs are `opencode-version`, `runtime` (`v1` or `v2`, selected explicitly), and `cache-hit`. Review-only runs (`review-only: 'true'`) skip the OpenCode binary cache, install the external `pr-review` skill, and use a disposable temporary HOME (including isolated XDG paths).

## Pull request reviews

The reusable [`opencode-review.yml`](.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml) runs the SHA-pinned external `pr-loop/pr-review` skill in an isolated `review-only` environment. The old bundled `/review-pr` command, agents, and orchestration are gone. The `/pr-review` prompt loads the skill through OpenCode's native `skill` tool; On v1, optional plain-text instructions narrow review focus; v2 accepts only an empty prompt or `/pr-review`.

Direct action or bot review-only calls require `use-bundled-toolkit: 'true'`, a full `pr-review-ref` commit SHA, and a concrete PR URL/head SHA. The reusable review workflow retains `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` as public inputs for compatibility; its review agent remains fixed, comment mentions are irrelevant to PR events, and the bundle is required. The action retains its restricted GitHub API adapter and verified App-token publication flow, which are needed to enforce read-only evidence access and a commit-bound `COMMENT` review. The restriction is an OpenCode tool permission boundary, not an operating-system sandbox.

The reusable review workflow defaults to `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, currently free for a limited time without a model-provider API key or account. Override `model` with another provider and supply credentials only if required. GitHub credentials are still needed for review operations; model availability and free-tier limits can change.

See [Pull request reviews](docs/pull-request-reviews.md) for usage, permissions, trust boundaries, and limitations.

### Sakura OpenCode v2 integration check

The credential-free Bats smoke test checks the synchronized catalog with the
pinned OpenCode v2 CLI, including the isolated review configuration. It does
not establish provider parity or send a Sakura request. The manual **Trusted
Sakura v2 integration** workflow can exercise a catalog model with a real key:
configure the `sakura-integration` GitHub environment and its
`SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY` secret and `SAKURA_MODEL` variable (a catalog
model ID without `sakura/`), then dispatch the workflow from the default branch. Restrict access to
that environment to trusted maintainers. The workflow checks out only the
default branch and never runs on pull requests. It asks the model to use the
read tool; a successful run requires a completed tool event and the probe
marker. The CLI may make more than one HTTP request to complete that single
interactive task. The harness suppresses provider output and classifies common
failures without printing credentials. Its five-minute deadline plus a short
shutdown grace period is separate from the catalog's provider timeouts. A
successful run does not by itself validate rate limits or the effective timeout semantics.

# GitHub runner event inventory

This inventory describes the reusable workflows at the base of #60. It is not a
claim that the action has a general v2 GitHub runner. General automation still
uses OpenCode 1's `github run`; the v2 path is review-only. The separate review
adapter has its own pinned-snapshot policy and is outside this inventory's
proposed mutation policy.

| Entry point                               | Current routing                                                                                                                                                             | Mutation considerations for a future runner                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pull_request_review_comment` created     | The bot job requires a non-bot comment author with OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR association, and a configured mention. The body is input to the model, not authorization. | Resolve the PR through GitHub, bind the repository, PR number, head repository, branch and full head SHA, check permissions, and reject forks and changed heads before writes. |
| `workflow_call`                           | Inherited non-review-comment events require a nonempty prompt; inherited review-comment events retain the trusted-author and mention gates.                                 | A prompt alone does not identify or authorize a write target. Define and validate a target for each supported inherited event before enabling mutations.                       |
| `workflow_dispatch`                       | The bot requires a nonempty prompt.                                                                                                                                         | Define a trusted target and immutable expected SHA; do not infer write endpoints from model output.                                                                            |
| `pull_request` opened or ready for review | The review workflow checks author association, non-bot author and non-draft status. It also exposes `workflow_call`, but its job currently runs only for `pull_request`.    | This is the separate review-only path, not the general mutation runner.                                                                                                        |
| `issue_comment`                           | The bot has no trigger for issue or PR conversation comments.                                                                                                               | Unsupported; restoring this trigger requires a separate security decision.                                                                                                     |

The bot checks out the event's default checkout ref at depth one; it does not
explicitly check out the PR head. When `use-github-token` is true it persists
checkout credentials and configures a bot Git identity. Otherwise general v1
behavior, including App token exchange, progress, publication, reactions and any
attachment handling, is delegated to `opencode github run`; the workflow does
not independently guarantee those behaviors. Neither the workflow's trigger
check nor its checkout establishes a safe v2 mutation target. Fork behavior and
token permissions also depend on GitHub and caller settings. A future runner
must make its own checks and must not execute checkout-controlled configuration
as trusted authorization logic.

The allowlist mentioned in #59's draft PR #163 is not present on this base.
When reconciling that PR, drop `issue_comment` from its v2 runner allowlist;
this inventory does not authorize it. The PR review-comment event is distinct
from an issue/PR conversation comment.

# Pull request reviews

The `opencode-review.yml` reusable workflow restricts reviews to eligible non-draft, non-bot pull requests opened by trusted repository collaborators, independently of the supplied model. It installs the external [`pr-review` skill](https://github.com/dceoy/pr-loop/tree/main/skills/pr-review) from `dceoy/pr-loop`. The bundled `/review-pr` slash command, dedicated agents, scripts, and local skill were removed.

## Invocation

The review workflow uses `review-only: true` and passes the pull request URL and exact head SHA from the event. The public `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` inputs remain available for backward compatibility: the review agent is always restricted to `action-pr-review`, `mentions` has no effect on PR events, and `use-bundled-toolkit: false` is rejected by review-only mode. The action uses `gh skill install dceoy/pr-loop skills/pr-review --pin <SHA> --agent opencode --scope user` to install just the upstream Skill under `~/.config/opencode/skills/pr-review/` at the immutable `pr-review-ref` commit, then invokes it using a plain-text prompt. The workflow loads the installed skill through OpenCode's native `skill` tool; it does not generate a TUI slash command or modify upstream `SKILL.md` metadata. The default `prompt` is `/pr-review`, which is normalized to review focus before that instruction is constructed. For free-form review focus, select `runtime: v1` and `opencode-version: v1.19.3`; the old `/review-pr` command is not supported.

Review-only runs require OpenCode 1.2.14 or newer and GitHub CLI with `gh skill` support for the OpenCode agent (tested with v2.104.0). GitHub CLI v2.90.0 has `gh skill` but does not support `--agent opencode`. The composite action validates the OpenCode version and immutable SHA, then invokes `gh skill` directly in isolated user scope; no custom installer or package manager is needed.

For direct action usage, set `review-only: 'true'`, keep `use-bundled-toolkit: 'true'`, and supply `PR_REVIEW_URL` and `PR_REVIEW_HEAD_SHA` via the environment, or rely on a `pull_request` event. Comment events require both explicit variables. For manual `opencode-bot.yml` runs, provide `pr-review-url` and `pr-review-head-sha`; unresolved targets fail before OpenCode starts. Review requires a model API key and `pull-requests: write`; the default OpenCode App token flow additionally needs `id-token: write`.

```yaml
jobs:
  review:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml@ab6604cc588b61690c4eae15b4a9682c5c47f011
    with:
      prompt: /pr-review
```

For a focused review with v1, use matching runtime and version inputs:

```yaml
with:
  runtime: v1
  opencode-version: v1.19.3
  prompt: Focus on security and regression risks.
```

The default review model is `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, currently free for a limited time through OpenCode and usable without an account or model-provider API key. GitHub token permissions and the default OIDC-based App token exchange still apply to PR review operations. Pass `with.model` to override the default and supply credentials if required. Free availability and rate limits can change.

## GitHub App token reuse

The token resolver (`.opencode/scripts/resolve-app-token.sh`) is preserved independently of the removed review command. The trusted `pr-review-gh.sh` adapter is installed alongside it under `~/.config/opencode/scripts/`. The review prompt instructs the external `pr-review` skill to route GitHub operations through the trusted native API tool and adapter. Review-only runs use the action-defined `action-pr-review` primary agent regardless of the caller's `agent` input. The v1 integration exchanges the OIDC token inside `opencode github run`. The v2 launcher exchanges it before starting OpenCode and holds the App token in memory. OpenCode and its descendants receive neither the App token nor the OIDC request credentials.

The adapter considers the v2 exchanged token and candidates from Git `http.*.extraheader`. Read-only requests never create pending reviews: with `use-github-token: true`, they preserve the caller's workflow credential; otherwise, they use the first candidate when present, or the existing environment credential when no candidate is found. Before publication, the adapter verifies a candidate with a temporary unsubmitted pending-review create/delete probe, then exports the verified credential to its child `gh` process as `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The token is not written to a file or emitted as output.

- **Default (`use-github-token: false`)**: publication requires a verified OpenCode App token; unavailable or mismatched identity fails closed. Read-only requests may use the available scoped credential.
- **Explicit fallback (`use-github-token: true`)**: publication prefers a verified OpenCode App token; otherwise it uses the caller's existing workflow token and its author identity. Read requests preserve that workflow token.

For review-only runs, call the native `pr-review-api` tool with a `request` argument containing a JSON string such as `{ "endpoint": "repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/NUMBER/reviews", "method": "GET", "paginate": true, "page": 1, "offset": 0, "limit": 4096 }`. In v1, the tool invokes the adapter through fixed process arguments and stdin. In v2, it sends structured requests to the launcher over a per-run loopback endpoint. The launcher executes scoped reads through the adapter and holds the review request in memory until OpenCode exits successfully. For publication, use `method: "POST"` with an embedded `payload` containing the commit-bound COMMENT review. Unknown fields, duplicate keys, invalid bounds and invalid payloads fail closed. No shell expressions, input paths or CLI flags are accepted.

GET responses contain `offset`, `next_offset`, `page`, `next_page`, `total_chars` and `content`. With `paginate: true`, each request fetches **one** GitHub API page (up to 10 entries); `page` defaults to 1. Reissue the same page at `next_offset` and concatenate `content` until `next_offset` is null. If `next_page` is nonnull, continue with that API page starting at `offset: 0`. A short API page terminates pagination; an exactly full page may require one final empty-page request. This avoids downloading all preceding GitHub API pages for each response slice. Commit `check-runs` and combined `status` endpoints also support pagination; their complete response objects are preserved, with continuation based on the `check_runs` or `statuses` array. Use `paginate: false` for other singleton or immutable endpoints. `offset`/`limit` bound each tool response to at most 4096 characters. Immutable `git/trees/<SHA>` and `git/blobs/<SHA>` endpoints provide frozen file evidence; blobs are decoded as UTF-8, while truncated trees and non-text blobs fail. Mutable API responses can change between slices, so revalidate their snapshot before and after reconstruction. POST accepts no output-paging fields. In v1 it returns a bounded review receipt, and the model verifies the persisted review through GET. In v2 it returns a queue acknowledgement. The launcher then verifies the App identity, submits the commit-bound `COMMENT`, and checks the returned review ID, state, and commit SHA.

The adapter accepts structured requests only through the native `pr-review-api` tool. Direct `gh pr` and `gh api` CLI compatibility, file-based `--input` payloads, and arbitrary CLI formatting flags are not supported. The internal subprocess is independently scoped to the review target and verifies commit-bound `COMMENT` payloads before any write.

Automatic formatters and language servers are disabled in review-only runs.

The v1 adapter resolves credentials for each invocation. The v2 launcher supplies its held credential only to trusted adapter processes. In either runtime, the App identity probe runs before publication and creates and deletes a pending review. Explicit workflow-token mode skips the App identity probe in v2. The review agent denies tools by default and allows only the upstream skill, trusted reference reads and globbing, and the native API tool. It denies direct GitHub/network tools, general shell commands, grep, delegation, repository edits and all checkout file reads. Repository content is read through frozen Git blobs instead, so checkout symlinks cannot redirect file reads to runner credentials. These are OpenCode tool permissions, **not an operating-system sandbox**; use trusted runners and grant `pull-requests: write`.

## OpenCode 2 review execution

OpenCode v2 is the default, pinned to `v2.3.0`. To use v1, select `runtime: v1` and a matching exact v1 release. Floating versions are rejected.

The v2 review path accepts only an empty prompt or `/pr-review`, and only pull request, pull request target, or manual dispatch events. It does not support `issue_comment` or `pull_request_review_comment` events. The bot workflow gates review comments on trusted authors and configured mentions, but the action can also be invoked directly and does not enforce those gates itself. Free-form focus is currently supported only by v1. Manual events require an explicit PR URL and full head SHA.

## Review contract and boundaries

Upstream `pr-review` freezes the base/head snapshot, validates findings against repository evidence, and publishes one verified `COMMENT` review by default. It never approves, requests changes, merges, or modifies repository contents. See [the upstream skill specification](https://github.com/dceoy/pr-loop/blob/main/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) for the authoritative policy.

Review-only runs use a disposable HOME under the runner's temporary directory, including separate XDG paths, and clean it up at the end. Existing runner OpenCode configuration and binaries are never removed. They disable project configuration and external skill discovery, and use a fresh OpenCode installation. They force the restricted review agent and its tool permissions instead of inheriting the caller's agent permissions. Review behavior remains in the pinned upstream skill; no bundled command or orchestrator is installed.

The upstream skill's default commit SHA is defined by the `pr-review-ref` input in `action.yml`. The reusable review workflow omits this input and inherits the action default automatically. Direct action callers and the bot workflow can still override it; an empty bot-workflow input also falls back to the default in `action.yml`. The post-release CI updates the action default to the latest stable `pr-loop` release SHA via the release-pins PR, without modifying workflow files. `gh skill` installs the specified pinned commit without npm lifecycle scripts or local YAML rewrites. The action checks that the destination is unused, required reference files exist, and the installed Skill contains no symlinks. Failure is terminal; there is no bundled fallback. The existing Bats CI job exercises the exact inline installation command with a real SHA-pinned install. OpenCode GitHub integration can separately add a completion comment.

OpenCode v2 uses `opencode run --standalone`. For bot replies to review comments, the launcher posts only the final assistant message from the CLI's JSON output to the thread root.

# Reusable workflows

`opencode-action` publishes two reusable GitHub Actions workflows under `.github/workflows`. Call them as jobs with `uses`, then pass action configuration through `with` and provider credentials through `secrets`.

The examples below pin the reusable workflow definition to a full commit SHA. Inside the called workflow, `uses: $/.` references the action at the repository root from the same repository and running commit, so the workflow reference also pins the action implementation without a second checkout or a separate action revision input.

## Manual dispatch

`opencode-bot.yml` exposes `workflow_dispatch` with the same inputs as `workflow_call`. `model` is required, and `prompt` must be non-empty for the job to run. It can be dispatched from the Actions UI or by API clients and integrations authorized to dispatch GitHub Actions workflows.

## OpenCode bot

Use `opencode-bot.yml` for `/opencode` and `/oc` inline pull request review comments, direct manual dispatch, or another event with a fixed `prompt`. On v2, the bot posts a reply only for `pull_request_review_comment` events; the launcher posts nothing for `workflow_dispatch` and fixed-prompt runs.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode
on:
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]

jobs:
  opencode:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-bot.yml@ab6604cc588b61690c4eae15b4a9682c5c47f011
    with:
      model: opencode-go/kimi-k3
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
```

For pull request review comments, the reusable workflow accepts comments only from `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, or `COLLABORATOR` author associations **and** requires a configured `mentions` phrase in the comment body (case-insensitive). Supplying the required `model` input does not bypass either condition. On non-comment events, a non-empty `prompt` is required.

## Pull request review

Use `opencode-review.yml` for automatic reviews on `pull_request` events. It installs the pinned external `pr-loop/pr-review` skill; its default `/pr-review` prompt loads the skill, while v1 also supports plain-text review focus.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```yaml
---
name: OpenCode review
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review]

jobs:
  review:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
      actions: read
    uses: dceoy/opencode-action/.github/workflows/opencode-review.yml@ab6604cc588b61690c4eae15b4a9682c5c47f011
```

This example uses the review workflow's default `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` model, which OpenCode currently provides free of charge for a limited time without an account or model-provider API key. To use another provider/model, set `with.model` explicitly and pass credentials if required. Free-model availability and rate limits may change.

This example assumes a trusted, same-repository pull request. For `pull_request` events from public forks, GitHub withholds repository Actions secrets and makes `GITHUB_TOKEN` read-only; Dependabot pull requests have the same restrictions. Private-fork behavior can differ when repository settings explicitly allow secrets or write tokens.

To focus the review, select `runtime: v1` and `opencode-version: v1.19.3`, then set `prompt: Focus on security and performance.` See [Pull request reviews](pull-request-reviews.md) for review behavior and security guarantees.

## Inputs

Both reusable workflows expose the action configuration plus a runner input, except that `review-only`, `pr-review-ref`, `pr-review-url`, and `pr-review-head-sha` are bot-only inputs. The review workflow always enables review-only mode and inherits the `pr-review-ref` default from `action.yml`. The review workflow retains `agent`, `mentions`, and `use-bundled-toolkit` for caller compatibility. Review mode still forces the restricted review agent, ignores comment mentions for PR events, and requires `use-bundled-toolkit: true`:

| Input                 | Default                                                             | Description                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`               | `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` (review); required (bot)        | Model in `provider/model` format.                             |
| `agent`               | `build`                                                             | Primary agent; review-only runs override it.                  |
| `share`               | `false`                                                             | Share the OpenCode session.                                   |
| `prompt`              | `''` for `opencode-bot.yml`; `/pr-review` for `opencode-review.yml` | Fixed prompt.                                                 |
| `use-github-token`    | `false`                                                             | Use the workflow token instead of the default App-token flow. |
| `mentions`            | `/opencode,/oc`                                                     | Comment trigger phrases; unused for PR review events.         |
| `variant`             | `''`                                                                | Provider-specific model variant.                              |
| `oidc-base-url`       | `https://api.opencode.ai`                                           | OIDC exchange base URL.                                       |
| `runtime`             | `v2`                                                                | OpenCode runtime generation (`v1` or `v2`).                   |
| `opencode-version`    | `v2.3.0`                                                            | Exact stable release matching the selected runtime.           |
| `use-bundled-toolkit` | `true`                                                              | Review-only mode requires the trusted bundle.                 |
| `review-only`         | `false` (bot only)                                                  | Install and invoke the upstream review skill.                 |
| `pr-review-ref`       | `action.yml` default (bot only)                                     | Immutable `pr-loop` commit providing the reviewer.            |
| `pr-review-url`       | `''` (bot only)                                                     | GitHub PR URL for manual review-only runs.                    |
| `pr-review-head-sha`  | `''` (bot only)                                                     | Full reviewed head SHA for manual review-only runs.           |
| `timeout-minutes`     | `60`                                                                | Maximum OpenCode runtime in minutes.                          |
| `runs-on`             | `ubuntu-latest`                                                     | Runner label for the called job.                              |

The default runtime is v2 with a concrete v2 release pinned in both workflow YAML files and `action.yml`; Renovate tracks v2 releases. To use v1, set `runtime: v1` and an exact v1 `opencode-version`, such as `v1.19.3`. Floating values such as `v1`, `v2`, and `latest` are rejected. Review-only runs on v1 require version `v1.2.14` or newer.

Direct `workflow_dispatch` on `opencode-bot.yml` uses the same inputs. Its input mappings reference the `workflow_call` definitions via GitHub Actions YAML anchors to avoid drift.

GitHub.com's `$/path` self repository syntax resolves to the repository and commit of the workflow where it appears, including when that workflow is called from another repository. These workflows use `$/.` because the action is defined at the repository root. GitHub Enterprise Server does not support this syntax.

## Secrets

Pass only the provider secret needed by the selected model. The default free review model does not require an OpenCode Console account or `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; unlike the review workflow, the bot workflow continues to require an explicit model input. The reusable workflows accept `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `SAKURA_AI_ENGINE_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `CEREBRAS_API_KEY`, and `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`.

`GH_TOKEN` is optional. When omitted, the reusable workflow falls back to the caller's `github.token`. With `use-github-token: true`, that fallback is limited to `contents: read` by the called workflow even if the caller grants `contents: write`. On v1, for code-writing operations such as `/oc fix this`, pass a separately write-scoped `GH_TOKEN`; otherwise GitHub API writes to repository contents fail with `403`. On v2, `gh` is unauthenticated (no token in the environment); the persisted checkout credential in token mode is what enables `git push` from the shell, and because it stays readable there, treat the token as exposed to the run and scope it least-privilege.

## Permissions

The reusable workflows request `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write`, `id-token: write`, and `actions: read`. A called workflow can only maintain or reduce the caller's `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions: the caller must grant the requested permissions, but its higher `contents` permission cannot override the called workflow's `contents: read` ceiling. A separately supplied `GH_TOKEN` is not governed by that `GITHUB_TOKEN` permission ceiling.

The examples keep `permissions`, `with`, and `secrets` under the calling job so their scopes are explicit: `permissions` controls the caller token, `with` configures the reusable workflow inputs, and `secrets` passes credentials.
